note: ADR-0011 3.2 and 3.5; bars set from the first measured run (see the PR). The core is a Jiles-Atherton loop in common/dsp's OutputStage (stiff supply, no driver clip), three sizes defined by a low-field corner (30, 12, 5 Hz with Rs || RL = 566 ohm across the winding) and a saturation flux (0.25, 0.6, 1.2 V s), 1.0 FS = 100 V. Response: unity at 1-20 kHz at every drive to 0.02 dB (the model has no leakage inductance or winding capacitance, so the top end is flat by construction); the gain at the stated corner within 0.15 dB of -3.01 dB at -70 dBFS (measured 0.08, the trapezoidal step and the Rayleigh-region slope; the corner rises with level, test_transformer). Iron laws, held as relations the physics gives, not as units: THD+N falls with frequency at 40 Hz > 100 Hz > 1 kHz by at least 20 dB between 40 Hz and 1 kHz; the magnetising current depends on flux alone, so (f/2, L - 6.02 dB) has 6.02 dB more THD+N than (f, L) to within 0.2 dB (measured 0.07); a symmetric loop has no even harmonics (H2 under -120 dBc; measured at the float's rounding) and its third stands 60 dB above. At the bass, the THD+N of a Jiles-Atherton core is not ordered by level (the loop opens, then saturates), reported. Aliasing: no oversampler, measured on tones from 1 to 19 kHz at 44.1, 48 and 96 kHz. ADR-0011 3.2's -90 dBc at nominal (drive 6 dB, -18 dBFS) is met by the line core (the default) and the large core; the small core, with the earliest saturation, measures -82.3 dBc at 44.1 kHz (14 kHz tone) and is held to its own bar, a departure reported in the PR. Hot (drive 24 dB, 0 dBFS) is held per core at the measured worst plus 2 dB. The zipper tone is -30 dBFS (the bar moves with it, checks.cpp): at full drive a -6 dBFS 100 Hz tone takes the small core into deep saturation, whose edges are the effect and not a step. CPU: class B, one stage per channel, no oversampling.
